text: We evaluated a contrastive pretext objective applied for 500 steps before weak-label fine-tuning, using qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student, across num_seeds = 3 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.52 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.69, with the weak-to-strong transfer accuracy measured at 0.58 (SE 0.02). The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.36 with a standard error of 0.11, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.23. Because the observed difference between this PGR and the baseline falls within two standard errors of the PGR estimate, these data do not establish that the pretext objective improves weak-to-strong generalization; the direction of the point estimate is favorable but indistinguishable from the baseline at this precision. With only three seeds, the standard error is itself poorly constrained, so the comparison should be treated as preliminary and re-run with more seeds before drawing conclusions.
